composition.story: Cross-validation hides one fold of the data, trains on the rest, then scores the model on both. Rotating the hidden fold gives five held-out scores. Overfitting shows up as a model with a tiny training error but a much larger held-out error.

aha.observation: The flexible model's training error is 2% but its mean held-out error is 24%. That 22-point gap is overfitting. The simple model's gap is only 2 points.

controls.label: Model
controls.presentation: Switches the variant; changes the train and held-out errors compared in the final state

states.label: Split into folds
states.sentence: The data is divided into five equal folds, so every example gets one turn as unseen data.
states.why: Folds make unseen data available without collecting more.

states.label: Hold out fold 1
states.sentence: Fold 1 is hidden. The degree-9 model trains only on folds 2 to 5.
states.why: The hidden fold must not influence training.

states.label: Score on training folds
states.sentence: The model is scored on the folds it learned from. It nearly memorises them.
states.why: A flexible model can bend to fit noise in its training data.

states.label: Score on fold 1
states.sentence: The same model is scored on hidden fold 1. Its error is far higher.
states.why: Noise it memorised does not repeat in unseen data.

states.label: Rotate the hidden fold
states.sentence: Each fold takes a turn hidden. All five held-out errors are high, so fold 1 was not a fluke.
states.why: Repeating the test shows the weakness is consistent.

states.label: Compare the scores
states.sentence: Training error is 2% but held-out error is 24%. This large gap is how cross-validation detects overfitting.
states.why: Good fit to seen data without good fit to unseen data means memorising.

states.label: Split into folds
states.sentence: The data is divided into five equal folds, so every example gets one turn as unseen data.
states.why: Folds make unseen data available without collecting more.

states.label: Hold out fold 1
states.sentence: Fold 1 is hidden. The degree-1 model trains only on folds 2 to 5.
states.why: The hidden fold must not influence training.

states.label: Score on training folds
states.sentence: The model is scored on the folds it learned from. A straight line cannot memorise noise, so error stays moderate.
states.why: A rigid model captures the trend, not the noise.

states.label: Score on fold 1
states.sentence: The same model is scored on hidden fold 1. Its error is almost the same.
states.why: What it learned also holds on unseen data.

states.label: Rotate the hidden fold
states.sentence: Each fold takes a turn hidden. All five held-out errors are close together and close to training error.
states.why: Repeating the test confirms the result is stable.

states.label: Compare the scores
states.sentence: Training error is 14% and held-out error is 16%. The small gap shows no overfitting.
states.why: Similar scores on seen and unseen data mean the model generalises.

1.reason: The fixed picture of folds, model, train and held-out scores and the gap answers "how does cross-validation reveal overfitting?" through the train-to-gap links.

2.reason: The aha state "gap" is the final step, so the stepper rests on the 2% vs 24% comparison until the learner moves on.

3.reason: The Model select swaps the variant, changing training error, fold errors and gap (2/24/22 vs 14/16/2), and Step changes the active regions.

4.reason: Active regions, callout targets, sentences and readouts all come from state fields, and the links and region values come from variant data.

6.reason: Narrative, state labels and the step control all use the same names (fold 1, hidden fold, training error, held-out error, gap), and the model name matches the degree in the sentences.

7.reason: Each state activates a focused subset of one fixed picture and the readouts are two or three values each, with the final state adding the subtraction as the formula, so there is no clutter.

8.reason: The numbers are correct (means 24 and 16, gaps 22 and 2, ranges match), but in the gap state the same values appear both in the region values and in the readouts, so they are placed twice.
